does: Cuts food into tiny, even cubes that melt into a sauce or sit as a neat garnish.

intro.what: Brunoise cuts vegetables into tiny, even cubes.
intro.why: It teaches precise cuts for vegetables that blend into a sauce or make a fine garnish.

how: Cut the vegetable into thin slabs, then into julienne strips.
Gather the strips into a tight bundle.
Cut across the bundle at the same spacing as the strips are wide.
For a shallot, halve it, make fine cuts towards the root and a few flat cuts into it, then slice across.

cues.text: Cubes so small and even that they look like coarse grains.
The pile stays dry on the board.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the knife back over the pile to make it finer, which bruises it into a wet mash.
mistakes.fix: Cut each piece once. If the cubes are too big, cut the strips thinner next time.

mistakes.mistake: A blunt knife crushes instead of cutting, so the shallot weeps and turns bitter.
mistakes.fix: Sharpen the knife. A clean cut stays dry.

quiz.question: Which result is the aim of brunoise?
quiz.because: Tiny, even cubes can blend into a sauce or make a fine garnish.

quiz.question: After cutting thin slabs, what comes before the final crosscuts?
choices: Cutting the slabs into fine strips.
Make crosscuts directly through the slabs before cutting strips.
quiz.because: The width of the strips sets the width of the cubes. Cut across those strips to finish the shape.

quiz.question: Which pile most closely matches the intended cut?
choices: A wet mash of crushed pieces.
Small, even cubes resembling coarse grains.
quiz.because: Brunoise should look like tiny, even cubes, almost like coarse grains.

quiz.question: Your cubes are too large. What change would improve the next batch?
choices: Rock the knife repeatedly over the finished pile.
Make narrower crosscuts but leave the thick strips unchanged.
Cut thinner strips before making the crosscuts.
quiz.because: Thinner strips make smaller cubes. Repeatedly chopping the finished pile can bruise it into a wet mash.

comes_after.why: A brunoise is a julienne cut across, so the strips come first.

variant_of.differs: Far smaller. The food is first cut into julienne, then across into cubes that cook in moments.
